introduction: This guide is about paper, ink and trust. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá will not be quoted without his hand or seal; Bahá’u’lláh’s amanuensis writes day and night, falls asleep over the page, and owns his slips; copies are compared, corrected and carried on foot across Persia; some papers are stolen, some forged, and the originals are said to be safe in a Preserved Tablet whatever becomes of the pages. Every scripture has such a history. Baruch wrote from Jeremiah’s mouth and saw the roll burned and rewritten; Paul signed with his own hand against forgeries and named his scribe; the Qur’án speaks of honoured leaves and a guarded tablet; Hezekiah’s men copied out proverbs; Shakespeare’s friends rescued his plays from “stolen and surreptitious copies.” The cautions are scripture’s own: the ass that carries books, the searchers of the scriptures who would not come, the letter written on hearts, and Emerson’s wish for a revelation of one’s own.
questions: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá accepts nothing attributed to him without signature or seal, and the rabbis praise whoever “says a thing in the name of him who said it.” Why does accurate attribution matter so much in a religion?
Copies differed and had to be compared; Shakespeare’s editors faced the same task. What does the readings’ frankness about scribal error do for your confidence in the text?
The Qur’án pictures an ass carrying books, and Jesus speaks of searching the scriptures without coming to him. What is the right relation between preserving a text and living by it?
The Book of Laws was not to be translated or circulated before its time; at Pentecost each heard in his own tongue. How do you weigh protection of a text against access to it?

Papers were stolen and forged, and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá answers that the originals are preserved in the Kingdom. Jeremiah’s burned roll was rewritten, and he speaks of a law written on hearts. In what sense can a revelation be lost, and in what sense not?
The amanuensis says “not a single word was from this servant.” How do Baruch, Tertius and Thucydides help you think about the people through whose hands sacred and historic words reach us?

outside.why: Correct copies of the Writings are to be gathered for a library. The Second Book of Maccabees remembers Nehemiah for the same work: founding a library, he gathered together the acts of the kings, and the prophets, and of David.

“Anyone quoting me must have authority written either with my own hand, or tablets signed with my seal.” Paul: the salutation of Paul with mine own hand, which is the token in every epistle: so I write.

Opinions were being circulated under ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s name. The rabbis made honest attribution a virtue with a reward: everyone who says a thing in the name of him who said it brings deliverance into the world.
The reader is sent to the amanuensis to learn what was intended. When Ezra’s book was read aloud, others stood by who gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading.
“Whosoever quotes any thing from my tongue ask him an authority.” Paul warns his readers not to be shaken by word, nor by letter as from us.
Whoever claims a tablet or cablegram “must prove it.” Letters of credentials were already the custom in Paul’s churches: need we, as some others, epistles of commendation to you?

“Any account without documentation should not be trusted, for even if true it still causes confusion.” Thomas Paine’s word for what reaches us at second hand: it is hearsay to every other, and they are not obliged to believe it.
Even the holograph must be examined “to ensure that not an iota hath been added, subtracted or changed.” Jesus uses the same smallest letter: one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law.
Nothing added, nothing taken away. Moses: ye shall not add unto the word which I command you, neither shall ye diminish ought from it.

Writings not confirmed by the Interpreter “cannot be trusted.” Socrates says why any text needs someone to stand by it: ask it a question and it preserves a solemn silence; it always needs its parent to protect it.

One word in a copy differs from the original: “exercise utmost care.” A psalm on the standard aimed at: the words of the Lord are pure words, as silver tried in a furnace of earth, purified seven times.

Scribes’ copies differed, and no one knew which readings were original; a printing was ordered. Shakespeare’s fellow actors gave the same reason for the First Folio in 1623: readers had been abused with stolen and surreptitious copies, maimed and deformed.

“What hath been revealed from God is truth without doubt,” whatever the scribes have done. The Qur’án offers consistency as a test of itself: if it had been from other than Allah they would have found therein much incongruity. What kind of difference between copies would matter?
Copies are to be given out only “after comparison and verification.” Paul: prove all things; hold fast that which is good.
Existing copies “must either be made to conform … or be rewritten.” Deuteronomy’s king must write him a copy of this law in a book out of that which is before the priests.

The readings spend great care on the exact words of a past revelation. Emerson asked his own age: why should not we also enjoy an original relation to the universe, and not a religion that is the history of theirs? What would the keepers of these texts answer him?
A printing made under an opponent’s influence is to be compared with a trusted scribe’s hand. Proverbs: he that is first in his own cause seemeth just; but his neighbour cometh and searcheth him.
A Tablet in the hand of a known scribe is “preserved, protected and ancient.” Moses had the finished book of the law put in the side of the ark, that it may be there for a witness.
“Do not change the passage, for there is wisdom in it.” Pilate, asked to reword the title on the cross: what I have written I have written.
A treatise “written during childhood” is to be read for its intention. Paul: when I was a child, I spake as a child, I understood as a child.
Not a narrative, nor a scribe’s copy: “it is by the pen of the Most High.” The tables given to Moses were written with the finger of God.
A forged letter is exposed by comparing hand, signature and seal. The oldest forgery in the Bible used a real seal: Jezebel wrote letters in Ahab’s name, and sealed them with his seal.
Tablets “written by the Supreme Pen in the Preserved Tablet” have not come down, and claims to hold them are false. The phrase is the Qur’án’s: a glorious Qur’án, on a guarded tablet.
“Strange stories attributed to me.” Nehemiah’s reply to an open letter full of reported sayings: there are no such things done as thou sayest, but thou feignest them out of thine own heart.
The amanuensis: “not a single word was from this servant.” The Second Letter of Peter on prophecy: holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost.

Words revealed, not composed. Socrates concluded of the poets that not by wisdom do they write, but by a sort of genius and inspiration, like diviners who say many fine things and understand none of them.
“He heard and wrote down what the Tongue of Grandeur spoke forth.” Baruch wrote from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the Lord, upon a roll of a book.

A servant takes down speech as it is spoken. Thucydides admits how hard that is and what he did instead: it was difficult to carry them word for word in one’s memory, so he kept to the general sense. What separates a transcript from a report?
Verses came faster than they could be written: twelve hundred in an hour. The psalmist: my tongue is the pen of a ready writer.
“All are powerless to write.” The Qur’án: though the sea became ink for the words of my Lord, the sea would be used up before the words of my Lord were exhausted.
The scribe nods off over the page and goes on writing. Jesus to disciples who could not stay awake: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.
“Occupied day and night writing countless replies.” Jethro to Moses: thou wilt surely wear away; this thing is too heavy for thee; thou art not able to perform it thyself alone.
Letters to province after province, “too numerous to mention.” John’s last verse: the world itself could not contain the books that should be written.

The amanuensis cannot keep up with what must be written. The Preacher’s tired aside: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh. Is abundance of scripture always a gift to its readers?
Tablets wait because “no scribe was available to make copies.” One scribe of the New Testament signs his work: I Tertius, who wrote this epistle, salute you in the Lord.
Copies are to be delivered and sent on to other towns. Paul: when this epistle is read among you, cause that it be read also in the church of the Laodiceans.
Letters go out unread a second time, but “signed and sealed.” Paul takes the pen from his scribe at the end: ye see how large a letter I have written unto you with mine own hand.
A whole book dictated in less than a day. The Qur’án to its Prophet: stir not thy tongue herewith to hasten it; upon Us resteth the putting together thereof and the reading thereof.
The Báb counts his books as proof. John on why his was written: these are written, that ye might believe.
“We did indeed change the Book of Joseph before.” The Qur’án: Allah effaceth what He will, and establisheth what He will, and with Him is the source of ordinance.
A book revised by its author. Jeremiah’s second roll held all the words of the first, and there were added besides unto them many like words.
Sections arrived “altered and corrupted.” Paul: we are not as many, which corrupt the word of God.
Verses changed “without knowledge and without warrant.” Jeremiah: lo, certainly in vain made he it; the pen of the scribes is in vain.
“The most beautiful script, on the most delicate paper.” Job’s wish for his own words: that they were graven with an iron pen and lead in the rock for ever.
The Báb’s words are to be written in gold. Proverbs: a word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in pictures of silver.
Gold ink for the text. Paul on where a revelation is usually carried: we have this treasure in earthen vessels. What does costly writing honour, and what could it obscure?
A book sent to a king, written in gold. The decree in Esther was written in the king’s name, sealed with the king’s ring, and sent by posts on horseback.
Clear handwriting, fine paper, permanent ink. Moses of the stones set up beyond Jordan: thou shalt write upon the stones all the words of this law very plainly.
Ink that will not perish with damp. Isaiah: write it before them in a table, and note it in a book, that it may be for the time to come for ever and ever.

A copy is to be made and compared “with utmost care.” A heading in Proverbs preserves the names of earlier copyists: these are also proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.
The scribe finds his own mistake and says so: “This servant erroneously wrote ‘this.’” A psalm: who can understand his errors? cleanse thou me from secret faults.
Tablets are read again in the presence to make sure of them. A book of the law, found in the temple under Josiah, was read before the king, and he rent his clothes.

“The people of God must make a mighty effort to preserve” the text. Jesus to those who had done so for centuries: ye search the scriptures, for in them ye think ye have eternal life; and ye will not come to me. What can perfect preservation not guarantee?
Salmán came on foot every year for forty years, bringing letters and leaving with Tablets. Proverbs: as the cold of snow in the time of harvest, so is a faithful messenger to them that send him.
An uncle served “with utmost truthfulness and trustworthiness” in passing on letters. Jesus: he that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much.
He was never “careless in recording the words of God.” Baruch, asked how he wrote: he pronounced all these words unto me with his mouth, and I wrote them with ink in the book.
Replies wait on a reliable post. Proverbs: as cold waters to a thirsty soul, so is good news from a far country.
Copies are to be made of every Tablet before delivery. The Qur’án on its own pages: on honoured leaves, exalted, purified, by the hands of scribes noble and righteous.
The Tablets “should be dispatched to all lands.” A psalm: the Lord gave the word: great was the company of those that published it.
Sent out, “they shall prove most beneficial.” Emily Dickinson: a word is dead when it is said, some say. I say it just begins to live that day.
“Divine verses have rained down like copious rain upon that land.” Isaiah: as the rain cometh down and watereth the earth, so shall my word be; it shall not return unto me void.
“The Tablets contained in these four packets should not be lost.” Paul from prison: bring with thee the books, but especially the parchments.
The packets must not go astray. Paul also knew a letter that cannot be mislaid: ye are our epistle written in our hearts, known and read of all men.
“Due to wisdom they were not all sent at once.” The Qur’án of itself: a Qur’án that We have divided, that thou mayst recite it unto mankind at intervals.
Some Tablets were held back for a later packet. Jesus: I have yet many things to say unto you, but ye cannot bear them now.
“Several successive months passed without any word being revealed.” Muḥammad knew such a silence, and the chapter that ended it says: thy Lord hath not forsaken thee nor doth He hate thee.
The Supreme Pen paused, and the servant was perplexed. The Book of Samuel on another quiet time: the word of the Lord was precious in those days; there was no open vision.
Some answers are sent; others “are recorded in God’s Book.” Malachi: a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared the Lord.
Laws scattered through many Tablets are gathered into one. The Preacher gave good heed, and sought out, and set in order many proverbs.
Glad tidings compiled “that all might attain.” Luke’s preface: it seemed good to me also to write unto thee in order, that thou mightest know the certainty of those things.
“All divine Tablets have the status of one book.” Irenaeus, about 180, argued that four Gospels and no more make one Gospel, as there are four winds and four corners of the world.
Bahá’u’lláh’s writings will not be added to the Bible. The Bible’s last page: if any man shall add unto these things, God shall add unto him the plagues that are written in this book.
Tablets “to such an extent that it is impossible to enumerate them.” The Qur’án: if all the trees in the earth were pens, and the sea ink, the words of Allah could not be exhausted.

Fine script is preferred, “yet now it is necessary that they be printed.” Byron on what print does: words are things, and a small drop of ink, falling like dew upon a thought, produces that which makes thousands, perhaps millions, think.
Whether to print depends “upon time, place, occasion.” The Preacher: to every thing there is a season.
The Bayán is to be published only after the book that abrogates its severe laws. Hebrews on an earlier covenant beside a new one: that which decayeth and waxeth old is ready to vanish away.

A well-meant translation is refused because such things “become a cause of differences.” Ben Sira’s grandson on his own: the same things uttered in Hebrew, and translated into another tongue, have not the same force in them.
The Book of Laws was not to be translated in its author’s lifetime. John is told at one point: seal up those things which the seven thunders uttered, and write them not.

“The holy language of Prophecy,” not to be put into other tongues. At Pentecost the opposite is the miracle: every man heard them speak in his own language. When does guarding a text keep it from those it was meant for?
“Permission for their dissemination has not yet dawned.” Jesus on timing and audience: neither cast ye your pearls before swine.
An original Tablet is worth five hundred tumans. Proverbs: buy the truth, and sell it not.
“Preserve and protect these Tablets with the utmost reverence.” Milton: a good book is the precious life-blood of a master spirit, embalmed and treasured up on purpose to a life beyond life.

Tablets are to be kept with honour. The Qur’án has a hard picture of keepers who do no more: the likeness of those who are entrusted with the Law, yet apply it not, is as the likeness of the ass carrying books.
The documents are to hang on the walls of the House of Worship, “not in a safe.” Jesus: neither do men light a candle, and put it under a bushel, but on a candlestick.
Papers in Bahá’u’lláh’s hand were taken and kept back. Jesus to the lawyers: ye have taken away the key of knowledge.
Writings appropriated, which “a single dot here and there” could alter. Jeremiah: I am against the prophets that steal my words every one from his neighbour.
Opponents “intended to destroy” two books because of what they foretold. King Jehoiakim heard three or four leaves of Jeremiah’s roll, cut it with the penknife, and cast it into the fire.
All who hold copies must guard them. Under Antiochus, when they had rent in pieces the books of the law which they found, they burnt them with fire.
A forged Tablet appointing the scattering of the Cause. Paul: though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel unto you, let him be accursed.
A Tablet was fabricated and attributed to Bahá’u’lláh. The Qur’án on that offence: woe unto those who write the Scripture with their hands and then say, This is from Allah.
The stolen books were only “a reflection of that Preserved Tablet.” A psalm: for ever, O Lord, thy word is settled in heaven.
The loss of the papers is not the loss of the word. Isaiah: the grass withereth, the flower fadeth: but the word of our God shall stand for ever.
The originals are safe in the Kingdom. Jeremiah looked to another place of safe keeping: I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts.
“Verses alone have been proof for all.” The Qur’án on who keeps them: We reveal the Reminder, and lo! We verily are its Guardian.

jeremiah-with-ink-in-the-book.text: And they asked Baruch, saying, Tell us now, How didst thou write all these words at his mouth? Then Baruch answered them, He pronounced all these words unto me with his mouth, and I wrote them with ink in the book

jeremiah-cut-it-with-the-penknife.text: Now the king sat in the winterhouse in the ninth month: and there was a fire on the hearth burning before him. And it came to pass, that when Jehudi had read three or four leaves, he cut it with the penknife, and cast it into the fire that was on the hearth

deuteronomy-in-the-side-of-the-ark.text: And it came to pass, when Moses had made an end of writing the words of this law in a book, until they were finished, That Moses commanded the Levites, which bare the ark of the covenant of the Lord, saying, Take this book of the law, and put it in the side of the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God, that it may be there for a witness against thee

kings-found-the-book-of-the-law.text: And Hilkiah the high priest said unto Shaphan the scribe, I have found the book of the law in the house of the Lord. And Hilkiah gave the book to Shaphan, and he read it. And Shaphan the scribe came to the king, and brought the king word again, and said, Thy servants have gathered the money that was found in the house, and have delivered it into the hand of them that do the work, that have the oversight of the house of the Lord. And Shaphan the scribe shewed the king, saying, Hilkiah the priest hath delivered me a book. And Shaphan read it before the king. And it came to pass, when the king had heard the words of the book of the law, that he rent his clothes

isaiah-note-it-in-a-book.text: Now go, write it before them in a table, and note it in a book, that it may be for the time to come for ever and ever

job-graven-with-an-iron-pen.text: Oh that my words were now written! oh that they were printed in a book! That they were graven with an iron pen and lead in the rock for ever

psalm-settled-in-heaven.text: For ever, O Lord, thy word is settled in heaven

john-these-are-written.text: And many other signs truly did Jesus in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book: But these are written, that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have life through his name

galatians-with-mine-own-hand.text: Ye see how large a letter I have written unto you with mine own hand

romans-i-tertius.text: I Tertius, who wrote this epistle, salute you in the Lord

corinthians-corrupt-the-word.text: For we are not as many, which corrupt the word of God: but as of sincerity, but as of God, in the sight of God speak we in Christ

esther-sealed-with-the-kings-ring.text: Write ye also for the Jews, as it liketh you, in the king's name, and seal it with the king's ring: for the writing which is written in the king's name, and sealed with the king's ring, may no man reverse. Then were the king's scribes called at that time in the third month, that is, the month Sivan, on the three and twentieth day thereof; and it was written according to all that Mordecai commanded unto the Jews, and to the lieutenants, and the deputies and rulers of the provinces which are from India unto Ethiopia, an hundred twenty and seven provinces, unto every province according to the writing thereof, and unto every people after their language, and to the Jews according to their writing, and according to their language. And he wrote in the king Ahasuerus' name, and sealed it with the king's ring, and sent letters by posts on horseback, and riders on mules, camels, and young dromedaries

kings-letters-in-ahabs-name.text: So she wrote letters in Ahab's name, and sealed them with his seal, and sent the letters unto the elders and to the nobles that were in his city, dwelling with Naboth

nehemiah-feignest-them-out-of-thine-own-.text: Then sent Sanballat his servant unto me in like manner the fifth time with an open letter in his hand; Wherein was written, It is reported among the heathen, and Gashmu saith it, that thou and the Jews think to rebel: for which cause thou buildest the wall, that thou mayest be their king, according to these words. And thou hast also appointed prophets to preach of thee at Jerusalem, saying, There is a king in Judah: and now shall it be reported to the king according to these words. Come now therefore, and let us take counsel together. Then I sent unto him, saying, There are no such things done as thou sayest, but thou feignest them out of thine own heart

corinthians-epistles-of-commendation.text: Do we begin again to commend ourselves? or need we, as some others, epistles of commendation to you, or letters of commendation from you

proverbs-men-of-hezekiah-copied-out.text: These are also proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out

ecclesiastes-acceptable-words.text: And moreover, because the preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge; yea, he gave good heed, and sought out, and set in order many proverbs. The preacher sought to find out acceptable words: and that which was written was upright, even words of truth

deuteronomy-write-very-plainly.text: And thou shalt write upon the stones all the words of this law very plainly

psalm-company-of-those-that-published.text: The Lord gave the word: great was the company of those that published it

proverbs-faithful-messenger.text: As the cold of snow in the time of harvest, so is a faithful messenger to them that send him: for he refresheth the soul of his masters

jeremiah-steal-my-words.text: Therefore, behold, I am against the prophets, saith the Lord, that steal my words every one from his neighbour

john-what-i-have-written.text: And Pilate wrote a title, and put it on the cross. And the writing was Jesus Of Nazareth The King Of The Jews. This title then read many of the Jews: for the place where Jesus was crucified was nigh to the city: and it was written in Hebrew, and Greek, and Latin. Then said the chief priests of the Jews to Pilate, Write not, The King of the Jews; but that he said, I am King of the Jews. Pilate answered, What I have written
